summary: Listed as a tower in Burke County, NC; a 2022 trip report and NC Tripping describe a stone foundation of an old fire tower on the summit.

facts.status_note: Tower gone; a stone foundation remains on the summit.

access.note: Summit reached on a hiking trail in Pisgah National Forest.

visit.trail_note: About a mile of climbing from the Table Rock parking and picnic area, most of it along the Mountains to Sea Trail.

evidence.quote: Table Rock is a mountain in the east rim of Linville Gorge

evidence.supports: managed as part of Pisgah National Forest, Grandfather Ranger District
evidence.quote: part of Pisgah National Forest (Grandfather Ranger District)

evidence.supports: foundation of an old fire tower on the summit (2022 trip report)
evidence.quote: see the foundation of an old fire tower

evidence.supports: stone foundation once used as the base for a fire tower; hikers can explore it
evidence.quote: You can also explore the stone foundation that was once used as the base for a fire tower.

evidence.supports: about a mile of climbing to the summit, mostly on the Mountains to Sea trail
evidence.quote: reach the summit of Table Rock after just about a mile of climbing

evidence.supports: 9.5 miles on a service road from NC-181, then a paved road to the parking area
evidence.quote: If you drive 9.5 miles from NC-181 on a service road

evidence.supports: four-wheel-drive vehicles preferred on the access road

notes_for_editor: No build date, builder, design, height or staffing found in any source read. The NHLR and firetower.org North Carolina indexes do not name the tower. The 2022 date for the trip report comes from its URL, not from page text. Wikipedia's summit coordinates (about 35.886, -81.8845) sit roughly 0.5 km from the tnlandforms point; not treated as a conflict. The 2013 Table Rock wildfire (Wikipedia) and a Tripadvisor review seen in search results are left out: no read source ties either to the tower.
